kurz: Meat is muscle: bundles of protein fibres, full of water, held together by connective tissue. Cooking means deciding how firm the fibres get and what happens to the connective tissue.
bild_im_kopf: Like a bundle of wet sponges in a net: squeeze too hard and the water runs out. Dissolve the net slowly and everything falls tenderly apart.
was_passiert: When heated, the muscle fibres contract and squeeze out juice: the hotter, the more. Connective tissue is tough but dissolves into gelatine in long, moist heat. On the outside, dry, strong heat creates crust and roasted aromas.
warum_wichtig: From this follow the two great paths: cook [[zart|tender]] cuts briefly and precisely; braise cuts with lots of connective tissue long and slow.
faustregeln: Quick frying for tender cuts with little connective tissue (fillet, entrecôte, rump).
Braising for cuts with lots of connective tissue (shoulder, shin, cheek, boiling beef).
A meat thermometer replaces any gut feeling.
